Examples: 24+12, 33+45, 51+26, 70+19, 42+35, 61+28, 15+54, 82+17. Constraints: Numbers within 100, no carries required, use regrouping-workbench.

sample.description: Students identify whether a word in a sentence represents a person, place, or thing by choosing the correct category for highlighted nouns. Focus: Identifying common nouns in sentences. Examples: teacher, school, cat, ball, doctor, park, desk, sister. Constraints: Use simple, decodable sentences. Provide visual clues for person, place, and thing.

sample.subject: Mathematics
sample.description: Compare two identical containers with different amounts using terms "more" and "less"

sample.subject: Social Studies
sample.description: Sort everyday items into "past" and "present" categories using picture cards

sample.subject: Science
sample.description: Perform stress tests on various geometric structures to observe which shapes hold weight most effectively. Focus: Identifying how geometric properties like triangle bracing improve structural strength. Examples: rectangular arch, triangular brace, square frame, hexagonal core, circular arch, I-beam shape, archway, truss triangle. Constraints: Apply virtual weight to each shape and observe failure points in the interface.

sample.subject: Science
sample.description: Drag the light source to different positions in the light-shadow-lab and predict the direction the shadow will point. Focus: Predicting shadow orientation based on light source position. Examples: top, side, below, diagonal. Constraints: Provide a clear reference grid for light placement.

sample.subject: Mathematics
sample.description: Sort various triangles into bins based on their internal angle measurements. Focus: Identifying right, acute, and obtuse triangles. Examples: equilateral triangle, right scalene triangle, obtuse isosceles triangle, acute scalene triangle, right isosceles triangle, obtuse scalene triangle, acute equilateral triangle, right isosceles triangle. Constraints: Provide visual angle arcs; allow rotating shapes for orientation testing.

sample.subject: Language Arts
sample.description: Students connect related words built from the same root word to identify their shared meaning. Focus: Recognizing base roots within varied word forms. Examples: care/careful/careless, play/player/playful, use/useful/useless, joy/joyful/joyless, help/helpful/helpless, teach/teacher/teaching, farm/farmer/farming, color/colorful/colorless. Constraints: Keep the root word spelling consistent to build confidence in morphological recognition.

sample.subject: Social Studies
sample.description: Distinguish between rules made for specific settings and laws that apply to all citizens. Focus: Identifying the purpose, scope, and authority behind rules versus laws. Examples: School classroom rules, speed limits on a highway, playground safety rules, city littering laws, cafeteria conduct, national tax laws, no-running zones, bicycle helmet laws. Constraints: Use a sorting activity to separate rules from laws.

sample.subject: Language Arts
sample.description: Expand simple sentences by adding descriptive words (e.g., "The big cat sleeps softly")

sample.subject: Mathematics
sample.description: Count the total number of items in each of the three sorted categories. Focus: Quantitative data organization. Examples: count of 5, 8, and 3; count of 12, 4, 7. Constraints: Total objects per category must not exceed 20.

sample.subject: Science
sample.description: Differentiate between living and non-living things in various environments with 80% accuracy

sample.subject: Language Arts
sample.description: Students use knowledge of common prefixes and suffixes to decode and construct the meaning of complex words. Focus: Identifying the function and meaning of base words combined with affixes. Examples: unhappy, rewrite, preview, playful, sadness, joyful, unbreakable, disagreement, formation, fearless. Constraints: Focus on high-frequency Grade 4 affixes; require students to identify the base word and the change in meaning caused by the affix.

sample.subject: Language Arts
sample.description: Outline a narrative story by identifying the characters, setting, and key events in chronological order. Focus: Structuring the essential components of a story before drafting. Examples: A dog at the park, A girl in the kitchen, A boy at school, A cat in the tree, A bird in the nest, A fish in the bowl, A spider in the web, A mouse in the house. Constraints: Use an interactive storyboard to label story components.

sample.subject: Mathematics
sample.unitTitle: Number and Operations in Base Ten
sample.description: Students compare two three-digit numbers using symbols to indicate greater than, less than, or equal to. Focus: Numerical comparison based on place value. Examples: 345 vs 354, 702 vs 699, 810 vs 801, 222 vs 222, 456 vs 465, 911 vs 191, 567 vs 568, 303 vs 330. Constraints: Focus on identifying the higher place value digit first.

sample.subject: Mathematics
sample.unitTitle: Number and Operations in Base Ten
sample.description: Solve multi-step division word problems and verify results using multiplication. Focus: Applying and verifying division steps. Examples: 200 items in 12 boxes, 500 pages in 20 chapters, 750 apples into 15 baskets, 1200 students on 25 buses, 300 toys in 12 bags, 450 miles in 18 days, 900 minutes in 24 segments, 600 cups in 25 cases. Constraints: Perform check by multiplying quotient and divisor.

sample.subject: Science
sample.description: Students predict the outcome of environmental shifts on an organism and assess the potential for trait adaptation. Focus: Predicting consequences of environmental change. Examples: drought impact on flowers, cold weather impact on animal camouflage, habitat loss impact on activity, soil nutrient changes. Constraints: Present 'what-if' scenarios where students must select the most likely biological result.

sample.subject: Social Studies
sample.description: Classify various government-provided services based on the primary community need they address. Focus: Linking government functions to specific community needs like health, safety, and education. Examples: public schools, police departments, health clinics, fire stations, libraries, public parks, trash collection, street lighting. Constraints: Use a classification-sorter to map services to categories of Safety, Learning, or Health.

sample.subject: Social Studies
sample.description: Students analyze how local climate conditions dictate and influence human behavior and regional economic activities. Focus: Explaining human-environment interaction through climate. Examples: Building insulation, seasonal clothing, irrigation needs, indoor vs. outdoor farming. Constraints: Use scenario-based problem solving.

sample.subject: Social Studies
sample.description: Sort various inventions and tools into 'Older' or 'Newer' categories. Focus: Distinguishing between historical and modern technologies. Examples: Candle, LED light, horse, airplane, letter, email, abacus, calculator, quill, ballpoint pen. Constraints: 8 items to sort, clear visual representation, feedback on correctness.

sample.subject: Science
sample.description: Show that light travels in straight lines by creating and observing shadows. Focus: linear travel of light. Examples: light source blocked by object, shadow formation, straight line paths, laser beam model, object placement, light obstruction, shadow size change, shadow orientation. Constraints: ensure the light source is distinct and path visualization is clear.

sample.subject: Language Arts
sample.description: Students map specific reasons and evidence to the points they are intended to support within a complex informational text. Focus: Structuring the argument by linking proof to claim. Examples: linking a study finding to an author's claim about screen time, mapping an expert quote to a point about animal rights, matching historical accounts to a claim about the cause of a battle, connecting a percentage to a point about climate data, linking a definition to a claim about technical concepts, matching experimental results to a point about chemical reactions, pairing a personal testimony with a claim about community service, mapping a source citation to a point about health. Constraints: Ensure the activity requires identifying the exact span of text that contains the supporting evidence.

sample.subject: Mathematics
sample.description: Draw various polygons on a digital canvas based on prompts that describe their required number of sides and corners. Focus: Translating geometric attribute descriptions into accurate shape drawings. Examples: draw a triangle, draw a rectangle, draw a pentagon, draw a hexagon, draw a square, draw a quadrilateral, draw an octagon, draw a trapezoid. Constraints: Ensure snapping tools are available to assist with line segment precision; allow only closed shapes.

sample.subject: Language Arts
sample.description: Dictate or write one sentence per picture to describe a personal narrative sequence. Focus: Combining drawing and writing to tell a simple story with beginning, middle, and end. Examples: First I went to the park. Then I played. Then I went home. Constraints: Accept dictated or written sentences; assess that each matches the corresponding drawing.
